elements.element: Customer is not prohibited or restricted from participating in competing or similar projects or otherwise dealing with alternatives to Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 continues to prohibit the Company for 12 months from participating in any similar Internet project involving Deerskin Products.

elements.element: Customer does not grant Vendor any exclusive or sole-supplier right.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 continues to grant HDI the exclusive right to use the Deerskin brand for a self-contained consumer website offering Deerskin Products.

elements.element: Any Customer exclusivity obligation is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: The restriction and exclusive right are limited to the capitalized category “Deerskin Products”; the prior extension to substantially similar products and similar companies was deleted.

elements.element: Any Customer exclusivity obligation lasts no more than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 applies only during the 12-month period commencing on the Effective Date, notwithstanding the Agreement’s potential renewal.

elements.element: Customer’s exclusivity obligations terminate automatically if Vendor fails to meet any service level under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: The added operative sentence states that the Company’s Section 6.1 obligations terminate automatically upon HDI’s failure to meet any service level under the Agreement.

elements.element: Customer’s exclusivity obligations terminate automatically if Vendor fails to meet any delivery date under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: The added operative sentence states that the Company’s Section 6.1 obligations terminate automatically upon HDI’s failure to meet any delivery date under the Agreement.

result.reason: The redline does not achieve the preferred position because it retains both a nonparticipation covenant and an exclusive brand-use right. It fully achieves the fallback by limiting the operative exclusivity to Deerskin Products and 12 months and providing automatic termination for either a missed service level or a missed delivery date. The changes are confined to the exclusivity scope, duration, and required termination triggers, while the unrelated term and termination-payment provisions remain unchanged.
